translationRepairs: Through his mastery of documents and the law (wen Wuhai), he became the chief clerk of Pei.
Through his mastery of documents and faultless administration, he became the chief clerk of Pei.

文無害 is a clerkly virtue meaning faultless handling of documents, not a personal name; the literal's parenthetical "wen Wuhai" invents a false person, and "faultless administration" restores the sense.
The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been looking after the people's interests!'
The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been profiting from the people!'

After petitions accusing Xiao He of forcibly buying people's land cheaply, 上笑曰「夫相國乃利民」 is ironic; 利民 means taking profit from the people, not sincerely looking after their interests, and the handoff of the memorials for apology confirms the sarcasm.
Everyone offered congratulations, but Zhao Ping alone came to offer condolences.
Everyone offered congratulations, but Shao Ping alone came to offer condolences.
The surname is 召 (Shào), not 趙 (Zhào); "Zhao Ping" misreads 召平, and "Shao Ping" corrects the English name while preserving the rest of the sentence.
Zhao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.
Shao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.
召平者 names the same man as Shao Ping; rendering him Zhao Ping confuses 召 with 趙, and the replacement keeps the Dongling marquisate intact.
Zhao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.
Shao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.
召平謂相國曰 again has the surname 召; "Zhao Ping" is the wrong romanization, and "Shao Ping" restores the speaker's name without changing the quoted warning.
